scenes.heading: Handling a platform algorithm change that tanks a client's reach

sents.d: Handling a platform algorithm change that tanks a client's reach
When performance drops through no fault of your work, how you communicate it matters as much as the fix.

Algorithm changes and reach drops happen to every account manager eventually, and are rarely something you could have prevented — proactively explaining what happened, in plain terms, before the client notices and asks, builds far more trust than staying quiet and hoping they don't check.

Having a general response plan (adjusting content format, posting cadence, or format mix based on what's currently performing) shows the client you're actively managing the situation rather than just waiting it out.

Setting client expectations early that platforms change and results fluctuate — rather than promising steady growth forever — makes these conversations much less stressful when they eventually happen.

take: Explain reach drops before they ask, with a plan.
